title: Chordal theme: adaptive weighting and compact grid contrast
creator: Evan Patel
description:
Problem: Several enterprise customers with strong brand palettes report that when switching to dark or compact density modes the console loses visual hierarchy: primary buttons and table highlights look washed out or collide with brand accents. We need a token mapping and component override strategy that preserves brand intent while guaranteeing readable contrast and consistent affordance at compact densities.

Goal: Introduce an adaptive 'weighting' layer in the token pipeline that adjusts accent luminance/opacity and edge treatments based on three runtime dimensions: brand vibrancy profile, console density (compact/regular), and UI surface elevation. This feature should: 1) maintain WCAG AA text/icon contrast for interactive elements, 2) protect subtle data-grid separators and row highlights in dense tables, 3) preserve micro-edge details on small buttons and pills (stroke thickness, corner silhouette), and 4) be implementable as a precomputed token profile per brand to minimize runtime cost.
acceptance_criteria: Define a token weighting algorithm and publish a mapping table that outputs revised tokens for: accent-foreground, accent-border, interactive-hover, table-zebra, table-row-highlight, button-outline at compact sizes.
Provide Figma mocks for light/dark/compact density showing primary/secondary/ghost buttons and a complex dense table (>=8 columns) with sample data and selected/focused/hovered states.
Prototype a CSS/JSON token bundle (two variants: standard and compact) and a short patch for the Console to consume a 'chordal' theme profile. Bundle documented fallback rules for unsupported brands.
Automated visual regression tests: baseline images for key combos (dark/compact with strong brand) and pass thresholds for contrast and color-delta metrics.
Engineering sign-off on feasibility and perf (precompute approach acceptable).
Include accessibility audit notes demonstrating WCAG AA or better for text and interactive controls in all rendered states.

2026-02-18 - Design exploration: produced three initial weighting curves (soft, neutral, vivid). Uploaded Figma frames: <https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/console-chordal-theme>.
2026-02-22 - PM sync with Priya Kapoor: agreed target release console-2026.03 for an experimental canary. Added acceptance criteria for visual regression tests.

2026-02-28 - Eng feasibility review by Carlos Nguyen: prefers precomputed token bundles per brand+density; flagged button-outline scaling as potential implementation detail that might need runtime CSS variables for animations. Linked PR template: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1567>.

2026-03-04 - Accessibility review request submitted to Jamie Rivers. Jamie responded with early notes: ensure focused outline maintains 3:1 contrast against nearest surface for non-text controls; suggested small increase to hover luminance for icon-button states in compact density.
2026-03-07 - Updated token mapping prototype (JSON) and dropped sample table CSS illustrating zebra and highlight deltas. Shared on Drive: <https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ChordalThemeDraft>.

2026-03-10 - Implementer notes from Maya Thompson: will ship as 'chordal' theme flag behind feature gate; needs a small API extension in the theming loader to accept 'density' and 'brand-profile' keys. Created engineering task ENG-22011 as dependency.
Next steps: finalize mapping table, convert prototypes to token bundles, coordinate with Eng to wire feature flag and add visual tests to the pipeline.
tradeoffs_and_notes: Brand fidelity vs legibility: Strong brand colors occasionally fail accessibility thresholds on dark surfaces. The chosen approach reduces accent saturation and increases contrast for interactive states while preserving color identity via hue preservation and relative saturation adjustments.

Performance: per-render computation would be expensive and error-prone. Solution is to precompute a small matrix of token bundles for (brand-profile x density x mode) and fall back to a conservative neutral profile when unknown.
Edge cases: very low-contrast brand palettes (deliberately muted brands) will get a recommended 'brand-boost' suggestion for customers; we will offer guidance rather than forcing visual changes.
Fallbacks: if a brand requests a strict mapping, tools will allow pinning of core tokens; otherwise the chordal delta will apply to derived tokens only.
Testing: Visual diffs will use combined metrics: pixel-delta thresholds for major components plus color-contrast checks for interactive text/icons.
